description: Leftover Tax Deeds from the annual sales are sold throughout the year through one-off auctions by the state. Parcel Fair tracks this type of tax deed as over-the-counter property since they are leftovers. You can locate these parcels year-round using the Map Search or List Search.
California counties auction non-redeemable tax deeds throughout the year on an as-needed basis.

Foreclosure properties in Colorado are sold throughout the year at auction. Colorado has recently implemented a new year-round tax deed auction process starting in 2025, some auctions are online and others in-person.
Connecticut sells tax deeds at auction throughout the year along with other foreclosure properties.
Delaware sells foreclosure properties throughout the year. Delaware sells tax deeds throughout the year with a 60-day redemption period and 15% penalty interest rate.

Florida counties auction non-redeemable tax deeds throughout the year on an as-needed basis using both online and in-person sales. Florida counties hold foreclosure auctions throughout the year as needed. Annual tax lien auctions for all Florida counties (18% max interest rate, bid-down auction format)
Hawaii sells tax deeds at auction throughout the year on an as-needed basis with a 12-month redemption period, 12% penalty interest rate.

Leftover tax liens are foreclosed on and sold as tax deeds using a sealed bid format (also referred to as "Surplus" sales). Tax Liens are sold at auction using a bid-down interest format with an 18% max annual interest rate, redemption periods vary by property type and range from 6 months to 36 months.

Foreclosure properties are sold at auction throughout the year in Indiana. Indiana counties offer tax deeds at auction on an as-needed basis. Spring Auction Season: Commissioner's Sales (120 day redemption tax lien) are a rolling inventory of leftovers that did not sell in previous Fall Auction Seasons (Treasurer's Sales)
Sheriff Sales and Adjudicated Sales of leftover tax properties occur throughout the year in Louisiana. Tax Lien auctions for each parrish occur throughout the year in Louisiana.

Maine offers property through foreclosure sales throughout the year on an as-needed basis. Maine tax deed auctions are held at the township or municipality (not the county) and are allowed to use various types of auction formats, including Bid-Down Ownership, Sealed Bid, and Premium Bid. Deeds are sold with a 2 year redemption period at an 8% interest rate.
Massachusetts tax deeds are sold at auction by local townships and municipalities year round, offering a 6 month redemption and 16% interest rate.

Missouri Post-Third (or fourth) sales include tax liens not sold in the first three sales and are sold with a 90-day redemption period. Post-Third sales are sometimes conducted in an auction format, and other times as over-the-counter purchases. Missouri First offering sales include newly delinquent tax liens to be sold with a 12 month redemption period and a max interest rate of 10%.
New Jersey municipalities (not counties) hold tax lien auctions throughout the year with October - December holding the most auctions (up to 90+ auctions per month)

North Carolina counties sell tax deeds at auction along with foreclosure properties. When a tax deed auction concludes in North Carolina the winning bids are available for 2 weeks under "Upset Sales" where another investor can outbid the winning bidder, causing another round of "Upset Sale" over the next 2 weeks and can continue for many weeks (or longer) until no upset bids are received.

Ohio sells tax deeds and foreclosures via Sheriff Sale auctions throughout the year (typically 100+ auctions per month). Only a few larger counties in Ohio sell tax liens - these are available as "Bulk Sales Only" to large-scale investors.
Oregon offers property for sale at foreclosure auctions online. Premium bid auction, non-redeemable tax deeds

Leftover tax deeds from the annual upset sales are sold via sealed-bid private sales throughout the year. Leftover tax deeds are sold at Judicial Sales with no redemption period. Unsold tax deeds from Judicial Sales are made available through Repository Sales (at auction in some cases and occasionally as over-the-counter purchases).
Foreclosure property auctions are available year-round in South Carolina.
Redeemable tax deeds are sold with a 12 month redemption period and a 12% penalty interest rate

Texas tax deeds are sold at county auctions with a 25% penalty interest rate and a 6 month redemption period for non-homestead exempt property, or a 2 year redemption period for homestead exempt properties.
Virginia tax foreclosure sales sell non-redeemable deeds at a premium auction format, usually in-person but sometimes online.
Washington sells non-redeemable tax deeds at premium bid auctions throughout the year. Washington sells foreclosed property throughout the year via Sheriff Sales.
All Arizona counties with tax delinquent properties participate in the annual tax lien auctions. Arizona counties hold tax deed auctions throughout the year on an as-needed basis.

Georgia Judicial Sales offer tax deeds at auction throughout the year with a 60 day redemption. Georgia Non-Judicial sales offer tax deeds at auction throughout the year with a 12 month redemption, 20% penalty interest rate.
Minnesota counties hold tax deed auctions throughout the year on an as-needed basis.

Only a few counties in New York sell tax liens, some only offer through private sales. Tax Liens are sold at auction with a 20% max interest rate and a 2 year redemption period. New York counties offer tax deeds at auction throughout the year on an as-needed basis.
South Carolina Tax Liens are sold at in-person auctions using a premium bid format with a 1 year redemption and a 12% penalty interest rate that accrues 3% every 3 months.

Most Alabama counties with delinquent tax properties participate in the annual tax lien auctions (new system) which issues a foreclosable tax lien at 12% max interest rate and a 4 year redemption period. Some Alabama counties participate in the "classic" or "old system" for tax certificate auctions, issuing tax certificates at 8% max interest, premium bid format, and mature to become tax deeds after 3 years.
Premium bid auction, non-redeemable tax deeds

Maryland counties hold tax lien auctions each Spring from March - June, Baltimore County typically holds their auction in the Fall (August or later). Leftovers are sold in some cases through re-offer sales or over-the-counter.
Nebraska offers tax liens at auction, typically from January through April. Liens have a max interest rate of 14% annually and have a 3 year redemption period.
New Hampshire offers non-redeemable tax deeds at Premium bid auctions
New Mexico counties sell non-redeemable tax deeds at in-person auctions throughout the year.
Idaho offers tax deeds through Premium bid auctions with no redemption period.

Nevada Tax Liens are sold with a 12% annual interest rate and a 2 year redemption period. Redemption period for vacant land is reduced to 120 days. Nevada sells non-redeemable tax deeds at premium bid auctions.
Tax Deed with 1 year redemption period, bid-down ownership auction format, 10% interest for first 6 months, 1% monthly after that
Wisconsin sells non-redeemable tax deeds at premium bid auctions, sometimes offering sealed bid auction formats as well.
Utah sells tax deeds at Premium bid auctions (some online and some in-person), and issue non-redeemable tax deeds.
West Virginia Tax Liens are sold in person at auction using a premium bid format with a 7.5% annual interest rate and an 18 month redemption period.
Alaska conducts tax deed auctions with no redemption through both in-person auctions and sealed bid auctions.
Iowa auctions tax liens annually on the third Monday in June - a few counties offer secondary sales in July or later.
Tax Liens are sold at auction with a 3 year redemption period and a 10% annual interest rate. Vacant land carries a 2 year redemption period.
Oklahoma sells tax deeds annually in June through in-person auctions. The state recently passed a law allowing counties to sell via online auctions.
Vermont Tax Liens are sold at auction using premium bid format with a 12% interest rate and a 3 year redemption period.
Tax Liens are sold at auction using either a premium bid format or a random selection of the winning bidder. Liens have an annual interest rate of 12% and a 1 year redemption period.
Tax Liens are sold at auction using a premium bid format with an 18% annual interest rate and a 6 month redemption period.
Wyoming Tax Liens are sold with a 4 year redemption period and a max 15% annual interest rate.

Michigan's annual tax deed auctions start in August each year. Counties with leftover tax deeds from the annual tax sale participate in a re-offer sale in early September. Counties with leftover tax deeds from the annual re-offer sale participate in a "No Reserve" sale each November.

All Mississippi counties with tax delinquent properties participate in the Fall auction season (late August). Leftovers from the Fall tax lien auctions are sold at auction the following Spring (April)
Counties in North Dakota offer tax deeds at auction each Fall with no redemption via in-person sales.
South Dakota tax lien auctions offer 10% max interest with a 3 year redemption period.
